prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Stronger economy, fairer society: the Liberal Democrats’ 2015 plan is a five‑year, evidence‑led programme to keep Britain open, green and outward‑looking while spreading opportunity to every community.

Responsible finances and prosperity for all
- Finish balancing the structural current budget by 2017/18, get debt falling, then let public spending grow with the economy. Use a fair mix of savings and taxes on wealth, banks, big business and polluters (no rises to Income Tax, NI, VAT or Corporation Tax rates).
- Raise the Personal Allowance to at least £12,500 (around £400 more off most people’s tax bills) and clamp down on avoidance/evasion.
- Back a high‑skill, low‑carbon, innovation‑led economy: double economy‑wide R&D, expand the British Business Bank, support SMEs, green finance and alternative lenders, and devolve economic power locally.
- Green growth at the core: legally bind a Zero Carbon Britain by 2050, expand the Green Investment Bank, treble interconnection, end unabated coal by 2025, grow renewables toward 60% of power by 2030, and pass five Green Laws.

Opportunity from nursery to 19 and beyond
- Protect education funding from early years to 19, extend the Pupil Premium, guarantee qualified teachers in every class, and set a national goal to end illiteracy and innumeracy by 2025.
- Expand high‑quality childcare to 20 free hours a week (from nine months to age four for working parents), extend free school meals to all primary pupils, and double the number of businesses hiring apprentices.

Health, care and family security
- Invest at least £8bn more a year in the NHS by 2020; integrate health and social care; expand access to GPs and community pharmacists.
- Deliver equality for mental health with the first waiting‑time standards and an extra £500m a year; transform children’s and perinatal services.
- Make work pay and protect the safety net: roll out Universal Credit, improve back‑to‑work support, enforce the Minimum Wage, promote the Living Wage in the public sector, and reform assessments fairly.
- Secure retirement with the permanent triple lock, simple single‑tier pensions, stronger auto‑enrolment and fairer pension tax relief.
- Support carers with a £250 annual Carer’s Bonus and new rights.

Homes, places and the environment
- Build 300,000 homes a year, including 10 new Garden Cities; create Rent to Own and Help to Rent; strengthen tenants’ rights; cut bills with a Green Buildings Act and a national home‑insulation drive.
- Clean up the air with Low Emission Zones, accelerate ultra‑low emission transport, expand cycling and public transport, protect nature with new National Nature Parks and a Nature Act.

Freedom, fairness and power closer to people
- Protect the Human Rights Act; pass a Digital Bill of Rights and a second Freedoms Act; safeguard free speech and investigative journalism.
- Replace Police and Crime Commissioners, focus on prevention and rehabilitation, tackle violence against women and girls, and adopt health‑led drug policies.
- Devolve power across the UK, introduce votes at 16 and STV for elections, reform the Lords, curb big money in politics, and strengthen local decision‑making.

Britain in the world
- Lead in a reformed EU, back fair free trade and security cooperation, meet 0.7% aid, pursue global climate action, and advance human rights.
